`readRepositorySourceFiles` receives an explicit repository, literal filename, source scope, excluded directories and repository bound. It reads authored files from materialized repositories or their parent-pinned objects. Native Git must be available on PATH. This source reader does not install or link package dependencies.


## Exact committed source and shared primitive ownership

Code production MUST depend only on Data/Code primitives. Exact source reading
MUST NOT require the Git umbrella's Networking consumers or a workspace install.
This existing service owns the native exact-commit reader and its pure Git command,
object, submodule and source-value codecs. The umbrella forwards its old public
subpaths to these same exports; there is one active implementation and identical
function/schema objects. The existing root `readRepositorySourceFiles` API and
its source bytes remain unchanged.

`./pinned-source-files` exports `createPinnedSourceReader({scratch, environment,
environmentForRepository, resolveSubmodule, rejectSelectedNonRegular=false,
maxRepositories=32, maxPaths=100000, maxBytes=67108864})`. It returns a reader for
`{repository, commit, scope='', selectFile, enterDirectory}`. Selection is explicit;
only exact committed regular/executable bytes and their source coordinates are
returned. Declared composed Gitlinks enter their exact pinned commits through the
caller's resolver; `update=none` and unselected mounts remain outside composition.
The caller owns absolute disposable scratch and repository credentials. This API
grants no access, installation, publication or branch-selection authority.

The exact-commit reader supports full lowercase SHA-1 (40 hexadecimal characters)
and SHA-256 (64 hexadecimal characters) identities. Each disposable object store
is initialized with native Git's explicit matching `--object-format`, and its
actual storage format is received before fetching. An ambient `GIT_DEFAULT_HASH`
cannot choose another format. Native Git still owns commit/blob verification and
refuses incompatible or unavailable remote objects; this does not translate
identities between formats or permit abbreviated revisions. A reader may receive
separate repositories of either format without sharing their stores.

Strict receivers set `rejectSelectedNonRegular:true`; selected unsupported kinds
refuse instead of silently disappearing. Defaults preserve regular-file-only
behavior. Raw Git tree paths decode with fatal UTF-8 before selection. Finite
repository/path/selected-byte limits and original command/authentication/hook
controls remain unchanged. `./git-command-codec`, `./gitmodules` and
`./source-working-copy-schema` expose the original pure functions and value
contracts, including their existing schema IDs, full-ref grammar and command
plans. They perform no effects themselves. All package dependencies remain empty.

V&V: native local Git tests must receive pinned bytes, executable modes, binary and
Unicode files, exact composed children and dirty-worktree isolation; distinguish
default selection from strict selected-symlink refusal; refuse malformed paths,
invalid UTF-8, missing resolvers and exhausted finite bounds. Existing pure command,
ref-grammar and module-codec controls remain applicable. A native working-copy
fixture receives the unchanged root API. The umbrella's full original suite and
an export-by-export strict identity test qualify forwarding, including schema
identity. Exact published primitive and umbrella APIs are then read back through
the original registry receipt and used by the ordinary Code CLI; source tests
alone do not establish consumer delivery.

**History extraction's actual host prerequisite:** The original native
`test/extraction-mappings.test.mjs` executes `git filter-repo` on a disposable
Git history; a Node/Git runner without that separately installed utility
cannot qualify this test. The original dependency-free source reader itself
does not call filter-repo for ordinary pinned-source reads. The public
repository-owned native receiving workflow pins upstream
[newren/git-filter-repo v2.47.0](https://github.com/newren/git-filter-repo/tree/6f79afc8c90c592a3052e6cc53c2ca8907515bca)
by exact Git source and executable blob before running the *entire* source
suite. No private Git Services CI quota, production history rewrite,
unverified shell installer, or npm dependency on unrelated Git tools is
introduced. Full-suite passing remains separate from publishing a new
registry package or accepting a real user Work request.

The original command codec's `gitExtractionPlan.rewriteMappings` accepts bounded,
explicit file and directory histories and their receiving paths. Unlike a
whole-directory extraction, one evidence file can be retained without carrying
its unrelated siblings into the scientific repository. Run the generated
`git filter-repo` command only in the existing shared scratch-clone procedure;
source repositories remain intact. The native extraction regression checks
history retention, exact bytes and excluded neighboring source. PTGAE and
manoomin Science are the original receiving consumers for this extension.


The pinned-source-files entrance also exports receivePinnedRepositoryCommitSync and readGitBlobObjectsSync for an owner that already holds a repository or its original bare cache. They share the asynchronous reader native fetch plans and binary codec. Commit receiving is blobless; blob reading is local-only by default, with explicit missing-selected-object receiving through the original origin. Both adapters keep finite time, path and byte limits and create no checkout, worktree, branch or copied code tree.
## Reviewed source for exact-path publication

The pure `readGitCommitPathsRequest` decoder accepts an optional
`reviewedSource: {revision, entries}`. `revision` is the original reviewed
non-null lowercase SHA-1 commit identity, never a branch name or latest alias.
Every selected path occurs exactly once, with either its reviewed
`{path, mode, type, sha}` or `{path, absent: true}`. Missing, repeated, foreign,
unsafe or ambiguous entries refuse. A present object needs a non-null SHA-1
identity and one standard matching Git mode/type pair: regular/executable or
symbolic-link blob, tree, or Gitlink commit. Absence carries no object fields.

Reviewed paths are canonical repository-relative literal paths: no empty/dot
segments, metadata directory, absolute/drive path, backslash or control bytes.
The returned reviewed carrier is copied and frozen, preserving the exact
identities and explicit absence after caller input changes. Existing requests
without this optional field retain their previous normalization and behavior.

This decoder performs no Git observation or effect. The source publisher must
compare these identities with the actual original reviewed revision and current
target, preserve unrelated paths and refuse changed preimages. Parsing alone
does not authorize deletion, source publication or any particular carrier kind.

## Disposable native source construction (version 1)

Requirement: a declared source producer that reads native Git must receive the
original exact commit as a genuine Git root. A directory of copied blobs is not
a working copy; inventing a commit or weakening the producer's committed-source
checks does not satisfy this requirement. This source owner, not a package
publisher, owns transient materialization from its already-acquired objects.

The callable reader additionally provides
`await reader.materialize({repository, commit})`. Version 1 admits only the whole
root containing bounded regular/executable files; Gitlinks, symlinks, special
entries, scoped selection and embedded URL credentials refuse. It reads every
source blob under the existing limits before invoking the existing detached
worktree command plan. This is disposable construction custody under the
caller's existing scratch ownership, not institutional `sourceWorkingCopies`
admission, a branch allocation, or a new credential grant.

The returned frozen handle contains `kind: 'git.pinned-source-worktree'`,
`version: 1`, `repository`, `commit`, `directory`, `entries`, `verify()` and
`dispose()`. Entries retain the original pinned-reader shape
`{path,mode,bytes,source:{repository,commit,path,object}}`. No credential or
repository environment is returned. Verification retains independent digests;
mutating returned evidence cannot authorize altered source. `verify()` checks
the exact root/HEAD, native metadata and every authored byte/executable mode.
Additional untracked generated products are allowed, but their qualification
belongs to Code and the publication owner, not to Git.

Materialization uses an isolated environment without inherited credential,
configuration, Git-routing, hooks or filesystem-monitor settings. Native Git
must use the prefetched objects without lazy fetching. The original bytes-only
reader still does not checkout anything, and its existing behavior is unchanged.

Caller lifecycle: retain the handle through installation, declared production
and authored-source readback. Call `verify()` before Code's result is accepted.
A publisher may subsequently rewrite its carrier manifest; `dispose()` checks
physical/native Git identity rather than immutable authored bytes, so that
intentional packaging metadata does not prevent cleanup. The caller must first
establish that every producer/reader process has quiesced. An uncertain runner
must retain the handle and scratch for reconciliation, not call `dispose()`.
Disposal is single-flight/idempotent and removes only this handle's exact native
worktree. Changed root, Git binding, HEAD or routing refuses cleanup and retains
the affected state. It does not prune another worktree or destroy shared stores.
The outer source owner may remove its disposable scratch only after all handles
are disposed and no workers remain.

Native verification covers exact detached identity and dirty-original isolation,
source-byte drift, mutable evidence, unknown commits, unsupported links/Gitlinks,
redirected scratch/worktree/source, HEAD drift, byte limits, unsupported scope,
untracked generated products, intentional carrier rewrites and duplicate cleanup.
Publication consumers must migrate by selecting this explicit operation only for
supported native generation, and qualify the original produced artifact before
claiming delivered publication capability.

Configuration is an independent precondition, not inferred from byte equality:
store initialization uses an empty Git template. Before materialization, the
existing store's bounded regular local config is parsed without includes and
must contain only this owner's inert bare-store/object-format and exact origin
promisor settings. Includes, filters, worktree config, attributes-file overrides,
filesystem monitors, other routing settings and alternate/graft metadata refuse.
A filter could execute a side effect while returning identical bytes, so later
source hashing cannot substitute for this admission check. Held configuration
and native routing controls are rechecked before verification or disposal.
Verification also compares the native index's complete stage-zero path/mode/blob
inventory to the original commit, because Code's source reader depends on that
index remaining at HEAD. Untracked products remain allowed; a staged deletion
or replacement cannot pass merely because the working file still looks right.

# Legacy capability retirement

The Leader's 2026-10-23 request is to revive information in
`lib/emsenn/services/561-group/lib/legacy` into living services. Review a
folder's capabilities briefly, find their living owners even when names,
package boundaries or repository mounts are malformed, and remove covered
legacy files. Lean material is explicitly deprecated. Git history supplies
recovery, not evidence of a replacement capability.

The service shall inventory an explicitly selected committed subtree without
walking the host or reading every source body. It shall retain exact Git
revision, path, object identity and executable/symlink modes. A retirement
shall name a capability, reason, exact selected source paths and either a
living implementation witness or explicit deprecation authority. Unknown
capabilities and meaningful unique information remain for integration.

Deletion shall affect only selected committed files whose index and working
bytes/modes still match that revision. Untracked files, local edits, Gitlinks
and paths reached through symlinks shall survive. Independent eligible files
shall proceed when another is held. The ordinary CLI shall support preview,
apply, and repeated receiving without recursive directory deletion.

Applying through the ordinary command shall commit that batch's exact removals
before returning. It shall preserve unrelated staged work and handle literal
Unicode, newline and glob characters in filenames. A failed commit shall be
reported as uncommitted with a failing exit status; another batch shall not
begin until that retirement is landed. Leader, 2026-10-23: "because you ddin't
commit your retirement, another agent restored it as possibly a glitch".

Acceptance: use this on the actual legacy collection; compare against the
existing body-reading inventory's work and whole-repository reference walk.
Test a covered capability, an explicitly deprecated one, Unicode/newline
paths, local edits, symlink escape, unknown paths and untracked siblings.
Keep source retirement separate from owner conformance and installed use.

The preexisting `retire-wave` v2 reconciles into mounted living owners and
does not move active code into legacy or edit workspace admission. Its assay
shall exercise that current contract: clean unique source integrates while
conflicting source, original custody and unrelated workspace files survive.

A named result destination with a missing/unwritable parent or an existing
non-file target shall be refused before source deletion or Git landing. A
caller must not discover an unusable receipt path only after the retirement
has committed. This requirement follows the actual 2026-10-24 receiving job,
whose four-file commit succeeded before its nonexistent output parent failed.

The ordinary retirement command shall optionally finish upstream source
publication in the same invocation. It shall pass only the reviewed cut to
the existing Fabrication maker, refuse stale reviewed preimages, and receive
the actual immutable merge. It shall preserve the local commit and any
completed external effect when receiving fails. Repeating the same request
and durable output shall reconcile the original publication without another
push or review. A local-only invocation remains available.

Before a new `--apply --publish` retirement removes or commits any source,
the service MUST qualify the selected original mode/type/blob preimages at an
actual advertised original remote commit. The accepted local immutable plan
cut need not itself exist at that remote. Retain both the reviewed plan cut
and the independently received remote source lease; never substitute local
HEAD for remote source identity. If remote observation, acquisition or any
selected preimage check fails, refuse before deletion or commit. Local-only
apply shall not require an origin or remote availability. A retained source
candidate or completed merge shall continue its original receiving path on
replay, without preparing a replacement candidate or push.

The same command shall optionally publish the retirement's plan, completed
result and explicitly selected supporting records through the existing maker.
The caller supplies their actual repository and the maker's reviewed-path
request; this service shall not implement another source publisher. Validate
that declaration and both receipt destinations before retiring source.
Keep the record-publication receipt outside its own publication cut, so its
merge identity never makes the published retirement result self-referential.
After a record publication retains an interrupted candidate, replay shall receive the original
candidate without rewriting the completed retirement result, recommitting
deletions or opening another review. Changed record bytes, a substituted owner
or a different path set shall stop that replay before any effects.

Batch preparation shall belong to this same command. Given explicitly reviewed
canonical plans, explicitly named supporting JSON records and exact output
custody, it shall assemble one canonical plan, an exact-input snapshot and a
complete existing-maker record request. Only plans with the same source owner,
legacy subtree and immutable revision may combine. Duplicate capability IDs,
overlapping source paths, changed evidence, absent deprecation authority and
incomplete publication preimages shall refuse preparation. Assembly adds no
capability judgment, authority, source publisher or installed-use claim.

Preserve original UTF-8 input bytes, their hashes and direct living-code
witnesses. Only explicitly snapshotted record witnesses may be replaced by
the assembled snapshot witness. Refuse output/input aliases, linked paths,
foreign output owners and changed existing prepared files before writing.
Preparation and replay must be deterministic, bounded and restartable without
overwriting another worker's data. Apply/publication continue through the
unchanged retirement and Fabrication operations, including ordinary recovery.
Completed retirement and record publications MUST remain reobservable when an
old explicit record-owner path becomes a symlink to the same physical Git root.
This recovery MUST preserve the original plan, input snapshots, result and
publication request bytes. It MUST NOT authorize a fresh retirement or source
publication through an aliased root. Completed publications MUST be received
from their exact immutable merge, without a new GitHub merge or push attempt.
A transient read-only receiving failure MUST preserve the last completed
receipt bytes and return the current observation failure separately, so the
same retained invocation remains retryable.

# Bounded committed-source retirement

Extend the existing reallocation service, preserving its allocation and
reconciliation exports. Git's native `ls-tree -rz` on an exact commit and
explicit legacy path supplies inventory. No directory enumeration or
whole-host reference search is needed for this mode. NUL-delimited output
preserves literal filenames. The existing reviewer supplies capability
judgments; filename/name matches alone never authorize deletion.

A plan uses the service's ordinary JSON carrier and lists capability groups
with exact legacy-relative source paths. Covered groups cite actual living
files; deprecated groups quote authority. All paths are confined to the
selected repository. Before unlinking, compare the selected commit's blob
and mode with the current stage-zero index and native worktree bytes/mode.
Reject symlink ancestors. Hash symlink target bytes without following them.
Derive the Git executable flag from the owner execute bit (`0o100`), as native
Git does; group or other execute permission cannot mask an owner-mode edit.
Do not recursively remove a directory, copy an archive, fetch history, or
rewrite source. Return per-path outcomes so held files do not block clean
ones. Repeated apply reports absent sources without deleting anything else.
Receiving after a deletion commit also reports absence when both index and
worktree lack the selected path. A recreated untracked file remains held;
committing retirement must not prevent processing the next capability group.

Evidence files are independently inspected by the reviewer and hashed in
the receiving result. Their existence is a source witness, not a proof of
semantic parity or live installation. The plan records those judgments and
their limitations. Source classification recognizes the estate's MTS,
Elisp, Racket, Scheme and Lean as code, rather than opaque binaries.
When writing the full result to a named output, CLI stdout contains only counts
and source identity; large per-capability witnesses stay in that result file.

The CLI's apply operation finishes by landing the exact removed/previously
absent tracked paths in Git. Recheck their original index identities and
worktree absence, then use native NUL-delimited literal pathspec input with
`git add -u` and `git commit --only`. Other staged work remains staged.
Already committed removals need no new commit; recreated files stop landing.
A commit failure leaves an explicit uncommitted result and failing exit code,
so the caller resolves it before starting another batch. The lower-level
unlink function remains available for controlled composition and tests.
If a hook or another actor recreates a selected file while committing, preserve
it and report `committed-with-recreated-files` with the actual commit and paths;
the CLI exits unsuccessfully so the caller reconciles those files before
continuing. A completed commit is never misreported as uncommitted.

The tracked-retirement CLI resolves and checks a named result parent and any
existing regular output file before invoking the unlink operation. Named
symlinks are refused without following their targets. Missing result
parents remain caller errors; the CLI does not invent a records directory.
These checks cover known destination defects, not later filesystem races.
The refusal leaves the source, index and HEAD untouched.

A witness may explicitly select another actual Git `repositoryRoot`. Resolve
its relative path only within that owner and use the same no-linked-ancestor,
regular-file, non-legacy and SHA-256 checks. Record its owner in the witness
receipt. Omitted owners retain the original same-repository behavior.

`--apply --publish --output=RESULT.json` composes the existing local retirement
and Fabrication's public source maker. Before its first deletion, source
preparation reads the original origin's advertised main commit and uses the
existing Fabrication/Git source reader to compare every selected original
mode/type/blob against that independently acquired commit. The accepted plan
revision remains the local review identity; the distinct remote revision and
origin become a retained source-preparation witness and the maker's
`reviewedSource`. A local-only immutable plan cut therefore does not have to
be fetchable from the original remote. Unknown remote state or mismatched
selected preimages refuses before local effects. Removed and previously
absent selected paths form the complete publication cut. This
service contains no GitHub publication or merge algorithm. Save the local
receipt before publication and the returned source result afterwards.
The receiving root is the plan's validated actual `repositoryRoot`, passed
explicitly as Fabrication's `packageRoot`; process cwd does not choose the
retirement or publication owner. The selected Fabrication0.4.15-dev.243
provider owns `git-objects.mjs` and its bounded immutable metadata transport.
Resolve that exact sibling from its public `git/github-candidate` selection;
do not copy its fetch/shallow/readback machinery. This is an explicitly
qualified internal supplier boundary, not a claim that the helper has a
published public export. Promoting that shared reader to a public API remains
a separate conformance concern.
Retain a failed receiving result's candidate and merge identity; on replay,
check the retained root and path set, then ask the same maker to receive that
candidate. No working-tree reinterpretation or replacement review is needed.

`--publish-records=REQUEST.json --records-output=RECEIPT.json` extends that
ordinary invocation after retirement publication succeeds. REQUEST contains
`repositoryRoot` and the existing maker request fields `paths`, `message`,
`push: true` and `reviewedSource`. Git Source Reading's canonical decoder
validates the request. Both the plan and retirement result must be selected
inside that actual Git owner; supporting records are explicit regular files.
Record paths cannot traverse links, enter legacy, or include RECEIPT.

Persist the exact selected file modes and byte identities in RECEIPT before
calling Fabrication. The result file is final before that separate publication:
its source-publication result goes only in RECEIPT. On replay, validate all
retained file identities and reuse the already completed retirement result;
continue the original maker candidate using the same shared publication path.
An unresolved record effect retains its own original candidate and leaves
the completed retirement source effect intact. No new GitHub algorithm,
source acquisition, repository census or cross-repository transaction is added.

The same CLI also accepts a `legacy-capability-retirement-batch/v1` input.
Its actual record `repositoryRoot` owns relative `plans`, `supportingRecords`
and five `outputs`: `plan`, `receiving`, `result`, `publicationRequest` and
`publicationReceipt`. `publication` supplies the existing maker's message,
optional candidate and exact reviewedSource. No field requests execution;
the existing CLI flags still select preview, apply and publication.

A pure composer validates the canonical plan declarations, common source cut
and disjoint selections. It retains exact UTF-8 plan/record text and SHA-256
in a bounded receiving snapshot, without promoting a review status. Explicitly
embedded record witnesses are rebound to that snapshot after their original
digest is checked; all other witnesses remain unchanged. The existing canonical
Git Source Reading decoder validates the complete three-record maker request.

Preparation reads only named regular files inside the actual record owner.
It validates every output and input alias before any write. The three generated
files are created exclusively, or reused only when byte-identical; result and
publication-receipt files remain owned by the existing CLI. A partial preparation
can therefore resume. Changed input or prepared bytes refuse before retirement.
No checkout, dependency graph, directory census, private dispatcher or alternate
source integration path is introduced. Pure counterexamples exercise mismatched
cuts, overlaps, authority and evidence failures; the ordinary CLI consumes the
prepared products on the actual pending legacy work.
A record-owner root alias is admitted only for retained, fully received
retirement and record publications, with all five existing output files and the
same physical Git root. Prepared bytes still pass the ordinary exact equality
checks. Fresh or incomplete custody retains the canonical-root requirement.
Completed source effects use Fabrication's existing immutable merge receiver;
uncertain effects keep its existing candidate-landing recovery. Historical
absolute addresses and receipt bytes are preserved rather than rewritten after
a workspace move.
Read-only reobservation never replaces a previously completed record receipt,
including when its provider is temporarily unavailable; its returned outcome
still reports that failure. New or uncertain effects retain durable progress
writes through the existing record-publication path.
